clue.text: Unpleasant film about posh college boy’s surrender

indicators.note: something placed about another surrounds it, so one set of letters wraps round the other

blocks.note: scum is a nasty film on the surface of a liquid
U means upper-class, as in 'U and non-U'
C is a standard abbreviation for college
B is the abbreviation for boy, as in registers of births

explanation.surface: A posh student gives in after sitting through a nasty film.
explanation.walkthrough: SCUM wraps round U and C to make SUCCUM, and B is added. The 's stands for 'is', linking the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To succumb is to give in or yield to pressure, the same as to surrender.

clue.text: Supporters on course upset over man in rage

indicators.note: to upset something is to tip it over, and in a down clue that turns the letters upside down

blocks.note: golf tees support the ball on a golf course
a man is referred to as he

explanation.surface: Fans at a racecourse are furious when their man is beaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supporters on course' sounds like racing fans, but the course is a golf course. In a down clue 'over' places the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: To seethe is to be inwardly furious, boiling with anger, which is what rage means as a verb.

clue.text: Exclusive group’s intelligence collected in evidence

indicators.note: things collected in a place are gathered inside it, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: IQ is intelligence quotient, a measure of intelligence
a clue is a piece of evidence in a detective story

explanation.surface: A secret society's spies gather information to use as evidence.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests spying, but intelligence here is the brainpower score used in psychology tests.
explanation.definitionFit: A clique is a small, tight circle of people who keep outsiders away.

clue.text: Hunk endlessly showing off’s ignoring the spirit of the game

definitions.text: ignoring the spirit of the game

indicators.note: without ends means both the first and last letters are dropped

blocks.note: the word with its first and last letters removed
to sport something is to show it off, as in sporting a new hat

explanation.surface: A muscly show-off is behaving badly in a match.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is'. Sporting as 'wearing proudly' is a different sense from the sporting in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsporting behaviour breaks fair play, disregarding the ethos of fairness in a contest.

clue.text: Business breaks embargo to get cured meat

indicators.note: something that breaks into a thing gets inside it, splitting it apart

blocks.note: an embargo is a ban on trade
CO is the abbreviation for company, a business

explanation.surface: A company defies a trade embargo to import cured meat.
explanation.walkthrough: CO for company is one of the commonest abbreviations for a business or firm.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacon is pork that has been salted or smoked, a classic preserved meat.

clue.text: Consolidate agreement

blocks.note: first meaning: a verb, to press together firmly
second meaning: a noun, a formal pact between parties

explanation.walkthrough: Reads like an instruction to firm up a deal; the two words are separate senses, with the stress shifting between verb and noun.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means press down and firm up; as a noun it is a treaty or pact.

clue.text: Prepared clean home for reptile

indicators.note: something prepared has been made ready by being worked on and rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone has got a tidy vivarium ready for a new pet lizard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prepared clean home' reads as a finished tank, but 'prepared' is the signal to rearrange the nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A chameleon is a colour-changing lizard, and lizards are reptiles.

clue.text: Note setter’s method

blocks.note: the setter refers to themselves as me
MO is modus operandi, a way of working

explanation.surface: Take note of how the compiler works.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is possessive on the surface, but here it just joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A memo is a short written message or reminder, a note.

clue.text: Making sense of a complicated pudding

indicators.note: something complicated is tangled and muddled, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is trying to follow the recipe for a fiddly dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks you to decode a recipe; the letters of 'a pudding' are what get rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: When a story is adding up, its details are consistent and it is making sense.

clue.text: Nothing wrong with high targets?

blocks.note: first meaning: a perfect score, with no errors in a test
second meaning, read literally: marks to aim at that are at the top

explanation.walkthrough: 'High targets' sounds like ambitious goals; the question mark flags the literal reading of marks placed at the top.
explanation.definitionFit: Full marks in an exam mean no errors were made, and marks set up high are literally uppermost targets.

clue.text: Gets out by cutting loose ties

indicators.note: a thing cutting into another goes inside it, splitting it
loose means not held in place, so the letters are free to move around

blocks.note: these four letters rearranged
by as in multiplication, three by four, written with the times sign X

explanation.surface: Someone escapes by slicing through the ropes that bind them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' looks like a link meaning 'by means of', but it is the multiplication sign X, which goes inside the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To exit is to leave or go out, so exits matches gets out in the third person.

clue.text: Went quiet when thrashed in competition

indicators.note: in places one thing inside another

blocks.note: a cup is a knockout competition, like the FA Cup
to lam is to beat or thrash

explanation.surface: A team fell silent after being hammered in a tournament.
explanation.walkthrough: Lam is an informal, slightly old-fashioned word for hitting hard, as in 'lam into someone'.
explanation.definitionFit: To clam up is an idiom for refusing to talk, shutting tight like a clam's shell.

clue.text: Doctor honoured fee, reduced for time of crisis

indicators.note: reduced means made shorter, so the word loses its final letter
to doctor something is to tamper with it, altering its arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
the word cut short by its last letter

explanation.surface: A GP accepts a smaller payment during an emergency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' is a verb here, not the GP of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Your hour of need is an idiom for the moment of greatest difficulty, when help is required.

clue.text: Old American tattooist on radio?

indicators.note: the radio carries only sound, so the word is recognised by how it is heard

blocks.note: a tattooist puts ink into skin, so is one who inks

explanation.surface: A veteran US tattoo artist is interviewed on air.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent the final R of 'inker' is silent, so it matches the ending of the ancient people's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Inca were a pre-Columbian people of Peru, so an Inca is an ancient South American.

clue.text: Outstanding, however victory’s overshadowed by own goal

indicators.note: what is overshadowed is covered by something else, so one piece is enclosed by another

blocks.note: still can mean nevertheless or however
OG is the football abbreviation for own goal
a win is a victory

explanation.surface: A great result, though the win was spoilt by an own goal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding' looks like praise, but it means unpaid. In a down clue, overshadowed means covered, so the victory sits within the own goal.
explanation.definitionFit: An outstanding debt is one not yet settled, money that remains due to be paid.

clue.text: List each time scrap’s put on dumper lorry

blocks.note: a ship that lists leans over, or tips
per means for each, as in ten pounds per person
T is the abbreviation for time
a ruck is a scuffle or scrap

explanation.surface: An inventory of every load of scrap metal loaded onto a lorry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'List' and 'scrap' look like nouns about paperwork and junk; they are lean and fight. A lorry is the British word for a truck.
explanation.definitionFit: A tipper truck has a body that tilts to dump its load, the same vehicle as a dumper lorry.

clue.text: Roux heartily tucked into poisson, potentially toxic

indicators.note: from the heart means only the central letters of the word are kept
something tucked into another is placed inside it
potentially means what could be, so the letters might form something else

blocks.note: the French word for fish, taken as written
the two central letters of the chef's name

explanation.surface: A French chef enthusiastically eats fish that might be dangerous, like fugu.
explanation.walkthrough: Roux is a famous French chef family, and poisson is French for fish. The combined letters are then rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Something poisonous contains poison, which is what toxic means.

clue.text: Thing to shift cold: a paracetamol initially and something warm to wear in bed

definitions.text: something warm to wear in bed

indicators.note: to shift is to move things about, so the letters change places
initially means at the start, so only the first letter is taken

blocks.note: these five letters rearranged
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
taken as written
the first letter of the painkiller

explanation.surface: A cold remedy: take a painkiller and a warm drink before bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Something warm' suggests a hot drink, another meaning of the answer, but 'to wear' points to the hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightcap is a soft cap once worn to keep the head warm while sleeping.

clue.text: Stand firm with exhausted teams over race vehicle

indicators.note: exhausted means emptied out, so the inside is removed and only the outer letters stay
turned over in a down clue means read from bottom to top

blocks.note: a rack is a stand for holding things
CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
the first and last letters only

explanation.surface: Tired teams refuse to budge on a question about a racing car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stand firm' looks like one phrase meaning hold out, but it splits into two pieces, and the whole string is then read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A stock car is an ordinary saloon modified for rough track racing, so it is a racing vehicle.

clue.text: Planned camping by lake on Scottish island

indicators.note: in an across clue one thing on another comes after it, so the first-named piece goes second

blocks.note: someone camping is sleeping in a tent
Iona is a small island in the Inner Hebrides
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A deliberate camping trip beside a loch on a Hebridean island.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'lake on island' puts the lake after the island.
explanation.definitionFit: Something intentional is done on purpose, deliberately, which is what planned means.

clue.text: Finally where to find a shoe mender?

definitions.text: where to find a shoe mender

blocks.note: first meaning: in the end, after a long wait

blocks.clueFragment: where to find a shoe mender
blocks.note: second meaning, read literally: a cobbler works over a foot-shaped iron form

explanation.walkthrough: A last is the foot-shaped block a cobbler uses to make or mend shoes; the question mark signals the playful reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means eventually, after delay, and also literally positions a cobbler at their workstand.

clue.text: Dozy fish turned up on top of pond with young

indicators.note: turned upward in a down clue means the letters now run from bottom to top
the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter

blocks.note: eels are fish
the first letter
Y is the abbreviation for young

explanation.surface: A sluggish fish surfaces in the pond with its fry.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' places a piece above the next.
explanation.definitionFit: Dozy means drowsy or ready to nod off, which is what sleepy describes.

clue.text: Break into computer of poor journalist

blocks.note: first meaning: to gain unauthorised access to a system
second meaning: a writer of low-grade copy

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one story of a struggling reporter breaking into someone's laptop; the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: To hack is to intrude into a system, and a hack is also a derogatory term for a mediocre writer.

clue.text: X axis range’s big when detailed

definitions.note: a noun phrase for an adjectival answer; the X axis is the horizontal one

indicators.note: read as de-tailed, meaning its tail, the last letter, is removed

blocks.note: your horizon is the range of your vision or experience
a synonym for big, tall, with its last letter cut

explanation.surface: A graph's x axis spans a wide range when every point is plotted in detail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detailed' seems to mean thorough; split as de-tailed it means lose the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The X axis of a graph runs left to right, flat across the page, parallel to the ground.

clue.text: Drive anxious mile to secure parking

indicators.note: someone anxious is agitated and unsettled, so these letters are stirred up
to secure something is to hold it fast, so one piece holds another

blocks.note: these four letters rearranged
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A nervous motorist drives an extra mile to find a parking spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drive' looks like motoring, but it is the verb to force forward.
explanation.definitionFit: To impel is to push or urge onward, as a motive can drive someone to act.

clue.text: Wear out old horse

blocks.note: first meaning: to tire or exhaust
second meaning: a worn-out, broken-down nag

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as working a horse to exhaustion; the word is also the green stone, a sense the clue avoids.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means tire through overwork, and as a noun it names a decrepit nag.

clue.text: Delighted by cockapoo running around hotel

indicators.note: running means moving about freely, so the letters are set loose
going around something encircles it

blocks.note: these eight letters rearranged
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone is thrilled by their dog racing round the hotel grounds.
explanation.walkthrough: A cockapoo is a cocker spaniel and poodle cross; its letters barely move, which hides the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Cock-a-hoop is an old idiom meaning jubilant or exultant, extremely pleased.

clue.text: Brief journal that is describing concept

indicators.note: to describe is also to trace round, as in describing a circle, so one piece encircles another

blocks.note: ie is id est, Latin for that is
mag is short for magazine

explanation.surface: A short article in a periodical sets out an idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Describing' reads as explaining, but in geometry to describe a shape is to draw round it.
explanation.definitionFit: An image can be a mental picture or idea, a notion held in the mind.

clue.text: Supplies back up with very naughty son

indicators.note: going back means travelling the other way, so the letters run right to left
naughty means misbehaving, so the letters will not stay in line

blocks.note: the two letters turned round
these four letters rearranged
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A parent backs up a badly behaved son by providing for him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back up' reads as support, but it splits: 'back' is the signal and 'up' the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To purvey is to provide goods, especially food, as a trader does, so purveys means provides.

clue.text: Flower acquires good height without effort

indicators.note: to acquire is to take in, so one piece ends up held within another

blocks.note: a lily is a flower
G is the abbreviation for good
HT is the abbreviation for height

explanation.surface: A flower grows tall with no effort at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' could be a river, something that flows, but here it is the bloom, and 'acquires' has it take in the other letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something lightly means doing it with ease and little exertion.
